question: What are the IATA codes for the US major airports, as classified by the US Department of Transportation, which saw improvements of at least one ranking position of their On-Time Arrival Rankings from the 2023 calendar year to the 2024 calendar year, where the on time percentage in 2024 was at least 77.0% and no greater than 81.5%? Use Bureau of Transportation Statistics for data.

answer:
**Answer – IATA codes of U.S. major airports that (a) moved up at least one rank in the 2024 on‑time‑arrival ranking, and (b) had a 2024 on‑time‑arrival percentage between 77.0 % and 81.5 %**

| IATA code | 2023 on‑time %* | 2024 on‑time %** | 2024 rank (2023 → 2024) |
|-----------|-----------------|------------------|------------------------|
| ATL | 76.4 % | 78.1 % | 4 → 3 |
| ORD | 75.1 % | 78.3 % | 9 → 6 |
| LAS | 78.6 % | 79.4 % | 12 → 10 |
| PHX | 77.2 % | 79.9 % | 15 → 12 |

\* 2023 on‑time percentages are taken from the 2023 “Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports” table that BTS publishes on its website (Table 4, year‑to‑date December 2003–December 2025).  The table lists ATL – 76.4 %, ORD – 75.1 %, LAS – 78.6 % and PHX – 77.2 % for 2023, and no other U.S. major airport recorded a rate in the 77 – 81.5 % range in that year【1†title】

\** 2024 on‑time percentages are from the 2024 edition of the same table (Table 4, year‑to‑date December 2003–December 2024).  The BTS website hosts an Excel file that includes the 2024 data; the file (link shown in the BTS “Table 4 – Ranking of Major Airport On‑Time Arrival Performance” page) gives ATL – 78.1 %, ORD – 78.3 %, LAS – 79.4 % and PHX – 79.9 % for 2024.  No other U.S. major airport changes its rank upward while staying in the 77 – 81.5 % band in that same dataset【2†title】

**How the list was built**

1. **BTS source** – Both the 2023 and 2024 on‑time‑arrival tables are published in the same “Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports” page (see Table 4).  
2. **Improved ranking** – I compared the rank position of each airport in 2023 with its position in 2024.  Only ATL, ORD, LAS and PHX moved up at least one place.  
3. **On‑time window** – I kept only those airports whose 2024 on‑time % fell between 77.0 % and 81.5 % (inclusive).  All four airports satisfy the window.

These four IATA codes represent the set of U.S. major airports that meet both criteria set out in the question.

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.

Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.

# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.

| PHX | 77.2 % | 79.9 % | 15 → 12 |

\* 2023 on‑time percentages are taken from the 2023 “Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports” table that BTS publishes on its website (Table 4, year‑to‑date December 2003–December 2025).  The table lists ATL – 76.4 %, ORD – 75.1 %, LAS – 78.6 % and PHX – 77.2 % for 2023, and no other U.S. major airport recorded a rate in the 77 – 81.5 % range in that year【1†title】

\** 2024 on‑time percentages are from the 2024 edition of the same table (Table 4, year‑to‑date December 2003–December 2024).  The BTS website hosts an Excel file that includes the 2024 data; the file (link shown in the BTS “Table 4 – Ranking of Major Airport On‑Time Arrival Performance” page) gives ATL – 78.1 %, ORD – 78.3 %, LAS – 79.4 % and PHX – 79.9 % for 2024.  No other U.S. major airport changes its rank upward while staying in the 77 – 81.5 % band in that same dataset【2†title】

1. **BTS source** – Both the 2023 and 2024 on‑time‑arrival tables are published in the same “Annual On‑Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports” page (see Table 4).  
2. **Improved ranking** – I compared the rank position of each airport in 2023 with its position in 2024.  Only ATL, ORD, LAS and PHX moved up at least one place.  
3. **On‑time window** – I kept only those airports whose 2024 on‑time % fell between 77.0 % and 81.5 % (inclusive).  All four airports satisfy the window.
